New articles are not being crawledGoogle: “Discovered – currently not indexed”. Google’s definition: it postponed the crawl because it expected to overload the site.
1,431pages, against 1,372 articles published Jul 25 – Oct 12
  1. Search Console → Settings → Crawl stats: check Host status and “By response” for 5xx, 429, 403 and slow responses since July.
  2. Cloudflare → Security → Events, filtered to verified bots: make sure Googlebot isn’t challenged, rate-limited or blocked.

EVIDENCE REVIEW

Do these issues really explain the missing pages?

Each claim was tested against your Search Console exports. Articles are compared only with others published in the same months, because newer articles index worse whatever else is true.

ClaimEvidenceVerdict
Google is not crawling new articles1,431 “Discovered – currently not indexed” against 1,372 articles published Jul 25 – Oct 12. Indexed pages fell from 2,007 to 1,911 while 1,372 articles were added.Confirmed · main cause
Variety.com copies don’t get indexedAppear in Google: 17% of copies vs 35% of originals (Feb–Jul); 0% vs 7% (Aug–Oct).Confirmed
Short articles index lessFeb–Jul: 27% of articles under 100 words appear vs 44% at 200–299, but only 37% over 300 words. Median length 168 words for articles in Google vs 146 for those not. The top 20 articles by clicks have a median of 194 words.Small effect
Longer articles would fix the indexing dropSince August, articles of every length are at 5–11% in Google. The 1,431 “Discovered” pages were never fetched, so Google doesn’t know their length.Not supported
The risk score predicts indexingFeb–Jul articles in Google: High 25%, Medium 33%, Low 40%.Supported
Sitemap problems stop indexingGoogle already knows the 1,431 URLs (“Discovered”), so the sitemaps aren’t blocking discovery. They do delay new URLs by hours and send dates Google can’t trust.Contributes, not the cause
Content quality alone explains the August dropThe share of thin or copied articles barely moved: 50% (Feb–Jul) vs 55% (Aug–Oct). Publishing volume rose to 501–548 a month.Not on its own
Placeholder H1 blocks indexingOriginal articles with it: 32% appear vs 35.5% for normal pages.Not supported
Broken SEO titles block indexing4.8% appear vs 5.2% for other articles from the same weeks.Not supported
Homepage pagination wastes crawl budgetOnly 72 such URLs known to Google, and Google’s help page says “there is nothing you need to do”.Not supported

What this audit still can’t see

  • Crawl stats. How the server and Cloudflare answer the real Googlebot. This decides issue 1, and only Search Console has it.
  • Manual actions. Two Google spam updates overlap the decline (Search Status Dashboard: Aug 18–21, Sep 24–Oct 7). The overlap doesn’t prove a link; the Manual actions report will.
  • The URL lists behind 1,431 and 532. Export them from the Pages report and drop them into “Add more exports” below to tag every article.
SITEMAP AUDIT

The sitemaps list the right pages, but they’re stale and send false dates

Checked: the sitemap index, all 7 child sitemaps, the news sitemap, HTTP and Cloudflare cache headers, and every URL against WordPress’s own post list. Seven wrong practices, two of them serious.

#Wrong practiceEvidenceWhy it mattersFix
1Post sitemaps served stale from Cloudflare
High		post-sitemap4.xml: cf-cache-status: HIT, age: 11414 (3 h 10 min) at 13:25 UTC. Newest entry 10:14 UTC; the 4 articles published 11:30–13:02 UTC are missing. Adding a query string still returns the cached copy.New articles only reach Google through the news sitemap and links for hours, and the post sitemaps disagree with the index.Cloudflare Cache Rule: bypass cache for sitemap URLs (rule below), and purge on publish.
2Sitemap index sends false dates
High		The index says post-sitemap.xml changed Oct 21, 13:24, but its newest entry is Apr 9. It says post-sitemap4 changed at 13:24, but the served file stops at 10:14.Google uses lastmod only if it’s “consistently and verifiably accurate”. False dates teach it to ignore them.Each index date must equal the newest lastmod in that sitemap. Look for a custom Yoast filter or caching layer that rewrites it.
3Article dates keep changing after publishing
Medium		2,666 of 3,873 posts (69%) were modified more than a day after publishing. 210 older posts were re-saved Sep 8–23 in the bulk title rewrite, and 103 old posts moved into post-sitemap4.lastmod should change only for significant updates. Constant re-saves turn it into noise and reshuffle which file each URL is in.Stop bulk re-saves. Don’t update the modified date for SEO-field, tag or category edits.
4robots.txt lists child sitemaps, not the index
Medium		6 child sitemaps are listed by name. post-sitemap5.xml (due around Oct 30) will not be.If the index isn’t submitted in Search Console, Google won’t learn about post-sitemap5.List only sitemap_index.xml and news-sitemap.xml. Submit the index in Search Console.
5Google News titles contain raw HTML codes
Medium		6 of 32 news:title values have &#8216; or &#8217; inside CDATA, e.g. “&#8216;Imran Khan’s Vulnerability…”.CDATA doesn’t decode entities, so Google News reads the codes literally.Decode HTML entities before writing news:title.
6Low-value URLs in the sitemaps
Low		/share/ (blank JavaScript redirect) in the page sitemap. /category/uncategorized/ (70 posts) and 7 categories with 1–2 posts in the category sitemap.Sitemaps should list only pages you want indexed.Remove them.
776 URLs spelled two ways
Low		The sitemap writes ₹ as %E2%82%B9; the page canonical uses the raw ₹.Google treats them as one URL, but audit tools flag a mismatch.Avoid ₹ and other symbols in new slugs.
Fixes 1 and 4: copy into Cloudflare and robots.txt
# Cloudflare → Caching → Cache Rules → Create rule "Bypass sitemaps"
# When incoming requests match (custom filter expression):
(http.request.uri.path contains "sitemap" and http.request.uri.path contains ".xml")
# Then: Cache eligibility → Bypass cache

# robots.txt: replace all Sitemap lines with these two
Sitemap: https://varietyindia.com/sitemap_index.xml
Sitemap: https://varietyindia.com/news-sitemap.xml

ISSUE 4 IN DETAIL

Article length is a small factor, not the cause

Word count was tested against your Search Console data. Longer articles do slightly better, but length doesn’t explain why pages aren’t being indexed. The only group worth acting on is very short briefs with nothing original.

TestResult
Did Google read the missing pages?No, for most of them. 1,431 are “Discovered – currently not indexed”: Google never fetched them, so their length can’t be the reason. Length can only matter for the 532 “Crawled – currently not indexed”.
Before August: share in Google by lengthUnder 100 words 27% · 100–149 33% · 150–199 38% · 200–299 44% · over 300 37%. Longer helps up to about 200 words, then stops helping.
Since August5–11% at every length. The August drop has nothing to do with length.
Indexed vs not indexed (Feb–Jul originals)Median 168 words in Google vs 146 not in Google: a 22-word difference.
Where the clicks goArticles of 150–299 words got 1,516 clicks; those over 300 words got 165. The top 20 articles by clicks have a median of 194 words.

ISSUE 2 IN DETAIL

275 articles are copies of Variety.com stories

When two sites publish the same text, Google indexes one and drops the other. It will almost always keep variety.com, the original and far stronger site. These articles are bylined to Variety India staff and set their canonical to themselves, so Google sees an unattributed duplicate.

Variety India articleVariety.com originalSame text
‘Digger’ first reactions split over Tom Cruisevariety.com/…/digger-first-reactions…100%
Jodie Foster says ‘F1’ seemed made by AIvariety.com/…/jodie-foster-brad-pitt-f1…99%
Oliver Tree dies at 32 in helicopter crashvariety.com/…/oliver-tree-dead…98%
Marvel’s X-Men reboot sets May 2028 release datevariety.com/…/x-men-release-date…96%
Ariana Grande debuts at No. 1 with ‘Petal’variety.com/…/ariana-grande-debut-petal…96%

Variety Australia already does this correctly

au.variety.com republishes the same X-Men story, but its canonical points to the variety.com original. Google then credits the original and doesn’t treat the Australian page as a low-quality copy.

Variety India uses a self-canonical on the same story, so Google sees two competing versions and drops the Indian one.

How this was measured: Variety India articles were matched to Variety.com’s 2026 sitemaps (14,836 URLs), then both pages were fetched and compared. 257 share 60% or more of their text; 18 share 30–59%. Some copies may have been missed, so treat 275 as a minimum.

Now: marvels-x-men-reboot-sets-may-2028-release-date/
<link rel="canonical"
  href="https://varietyindia.com/marvels-x-men-reboot-sets-may-2028-release-date/" />
Fix: point to the original
<link rel="canonical"
  href="https://variety.com/2026/film/news/x-men-release-date-marvel-reboot-1236816959/" />

Fix: for each syndicated story, choose one of two options.

  • Keep it as syndication: set the canonical to the Variety.com URL (Yoast’s “Canonical URL” field, or set it automatically when importing from the Variety feed). The page stays live for readers, but Google indexes the original. This stops these pages from lowering how Google rates the whole site.
  • Make it a Variety India story: rewrite it with an India angle (Indian release dates, box office, local reaction), keep the self-canonical, and credit Variety.com in the text. Only these will index under varietyindia.com.

ISSUES 5 AND 6 · LOW PRIORITY

312 articles have “news-old-title” as their main heading

On these pages the only H1 is a hidden placeholder, and the real headline is an H2. 253 of them are the Variety.com copies above, so this is the template for imported stories. Tested against Search Console, the placeholder itself makes no measurable difference to indexing (32% vs 35.5%), so this is a cleanup, not a cause.

Now (e.g. the Jodie Foster article)
<h1 class="sr-only">news-old-title</h1>
<h2 class="details-titles">Jodie Foster Says Brad Pitt’s
  ‘F1’ Seemed Like It Was Made by AI…</h2>
Fix in the theme template
<h1 class="details-titles">Jodie Foster Says Brad Pitt’s
  ‘F1’ Seemed Like It Was Made by AI…</h1>

Broken SEO titles. Separately, 83 articles had their SEO title and description replaced with a template between Sep 8 and 23, 2026, e.g. “Ramayana: Latest Entertainment News & Details News News”. Seven articles now share one title, which makes them look like duplicates. Restore the real headlines and find the tool that did this.

Fix: one change in the theme file that renders the “news-old” layout fixes all 312 at once. Then restore the 83 titles.

Homepage pagination and the /share/ page

Both are untidy, but Search Console shows they barely register: 72 “Alternate page with proper canonical tag” URLs (Google says no action is needed) and 2 soft 404s. Fix them when convenient.

Homepage pagination Low priority

12…387388 empty, 2005000, 20099999, 200no end
Articles stop at page 387, but every page number returns 200 and sets its canonical to the homepage. Fix: self-canonical on each /page/N/, and a 404 after the last real page.

Sitemap fixes, including the robots.txt change, are in the sitemap audit above.

Also remove the blank /share/ redirect page from the page sitemap and give it noindex; every shared /share/?p= link is an empty page to Google.

PLAN

How to get articles indexed

First find out why Google stopped crawling new articles, then stop the copies and empty briefs, then clean up the archive. Tick items as you go; ticks are saved in this browser.

This weekDeveloper + SEO
Week 1–2Editorial + developer
Week 2–8Editorial
When convenientDeveloper + editorial
Every weekSEO team

Avoid

  • Paid “instant indexer” tools, or the Google Indexing API for articles. The API is only for job postings and livestream events.
  • Resubmitting sitemaps or mass-requesting indexing as the fix. Google already knows these URLs; it is choosing not to crawl them.
  • Mass-deleting or noindexing old articles before checking which ones get Search Console clicks.
